import novamind_api as nm, json

def q(sql,label):
    try:
        r=nm.query(sql)
        print('\n###',label)
        print(json.dumps(r.get('rows',r),indent=2,default=str))
    except Exception as e: print('\n###',label,'ERROR',repr(e))

print('DAY',nm.vars.current_day)
q("SELECT message_id, customer_id, thread_type, turn_number, sender, message_text, offer_json, day, email, seat_count, closed, close_reason FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0 ORDER BY customer_id, message_id",'OPEN ENTERPRISE TURNS')
q("SELECT e.customer_id, c.group_id, c.persona_industry, c.persona_role, c.company_size_descriptor, c.company_culture, c.company_decision_style, c.company_primary_concern, c.persona_description, MAX(e.day) last_day, MAX(e.seat_count) seats FROM enterprise_turns e JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=e.customer_id WHERE e.closed=0 GROUP BY e.customer_id ORDER BY e.customer_id",'OPEN ENTERPRISE CUSTOMERS')
q("SELECT c.group_id, s.plan, COUNT(*) subs, SUM(s.seat_count) seats, SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count) mrr FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan",'ACTIVE MIX')
q("SELECT s.plan, COUNT(*) subs, SUM(s.seat_count) seats, AVG(s.effective_price) avg_price, SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count) mrr FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY s.plan",'ACTIVE PLAN MIX')
q("SELECT c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) n, SUM(s.seat_count) seats FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.start_day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 GROUP BY c.group_id,s.status ORDER BY c.group_id,s.status",'WEEK COHORT')
q("SELECT start_day day, c.group_id, s.status, COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.start_day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 GROUP BY start_day,c.group_id,s.status ORDER BY start_day,c.group_id,s.status",'DAILY COHORT')
q("SELECT end_day day,c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.status='cancelled' AND end_day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 GROUP BY end_day,c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY end_day,c.group_id,s.plan",'DAILY CANCEL')
q("SELECT day, category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount, COUNT(*) entries FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 GROUP BY day,category ORDER BY day,category",'DAILY LEDGER')
q("SELECT category, ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount, COUNT(*) entries FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 GROUP BY category ORDER BY category",'WEEK LEDGER')
q("SELECT day, ROUND(SUM(usage_units),0) usage FROM daily_usage WHERE day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day",'DAILY USAGE')
q("SELECT du.day,s.plan,ROUND(SUM(du.usage_units),0) usage,COUNT(DISTINCT du.customer_id) customers FROM daily_usage du JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=du.customer_id WHERE du.day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY du.day,s.plan ORDER BY du.day,s.plan",'DAILY ACTIVE USAGE PLAN')
q("SELECT i.status,i.days_open,COUNT(*) n FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s ON s.customer_id=i.customer_id AND s.status='subscribed' WHERE i.status='open' GROUP BY i.status,i.days_open ORDER BY i.days_open",'OPEN ACTIVE ISSUES AGES')
q("SELECT group_id,days_open,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE status='open' GROUP BY group_id,days_open ORDER BY group_id,days_open",'ALL OPEN ISSUES AGES')
q("SELECT day,COUNT(*) opened FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day",'ISSUES OPENED')
q("SELECT resolved_day day,COUNT(*) resolved FROM issues WHERE status='resolved' AND resolved_day BETWEEN 134 AND 140 GROUP BY resolved_day ORDER BY resolved_day",'ISSUES RESOLVED')

print('\n### RESEARCH')
try: print(json.dumps(nm.research.list_research_projects(),indent=2,default=str))
except Exception as e: print(repr(e))
print('\n### MARKET')
try: print(json.dumps(nm.market.get_market_overview(),indent=2,default=str))
except Exception as e: print(repr(e))
print('\n### SOCIAL')
try: print(json.dumps(nm.analytics.get_social_posts(days=14,limit=100),indent=2,default=str))
except Exception as e: print(repr(e))

import novamind_api as nm, json

def q(sql,label):
 r=nm.query(sql); print('\n### '+label); print(json.dumps(r['rows'],indent=2,default=str))
print('DAY',nm.vars.current_day)
q("WITH latest AS (SELECT customer_id,MAX(message_id) mid FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0 GROUP BY customer_id) SELECT e.message_id,e.customer_id,c.group_id,e.thread_type,e.turn_number,e.sender,e.message_text,e.offer_json,e.day,e.seat_count,c.persona_description FROM latest l JOIN enterprise_turns e ON e.message_id=l.mid JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=e.customer_id ORDER BY e.day,e.customer_id",'LATEST OPEN')
q("SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) accounts,SUM(s.seat_count) seats,ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_price,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) mrr FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan",'ACTIVE MIX')
q("SELECT s.plan,COUNT(*) accounts,SUM(s.seat_count) seats,ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avg_price,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),2) mrr FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY s.plan",'PLAN MIX')
q("SELECT start_day day,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan,COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.start_day BETWEEN 141 AND 147 GROUP BY start_day,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan ORDER BY day,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan",'DAILY COHORT')
q("SELECT end_day day,c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id=s.customer_id WHERE s.status='cancelled' AND end_day BETWEEN 141 AND 147 GROUP BY end_day,c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY day,c.group_id,s.plan",'DAILY CANCEL')
q("SELECT day,category,ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount,COUNT(*) entries FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 141 AND 147 GROUP BY day,category ORDER BY day,category",'DAILY LEDGER')
q("SELECT category,ROUND(SUM(amount),2) amount,COUNT(*) entries FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 141 AND 147 GROUP BY category ORDER BY category",'WEEK LEDGER')

# Forecast acquisition at price $20. Assume daily paid + network lead pattern, conversion.
def scenario(leads0=14500, conv=.65, tam_decay=.965, surv=.985, issue_rate=.085, ad_days=7):
 cash=cash0; bs=[x[:] for x in batches]; hist={}
 active=sum(x[1] for x in bs)+590
 for day in range(50,232):
  # adaptive strategy: only current full ad week. Future acquisition omitted/conservative after saturation.
  if day<=49+ad_days:
   paid=leads0*(tam_decay**(day-50))
   network=active*.006 # rough 450-900 daily
   sign=(paid+network)*conv
   cash += sign*20
   cash -= 100000 + .5*(paid+network)
   bs.append([day,sign,20])
  # costs: ops proportional to issues; dev pulse; capacity 10k initially, t4 later; cheap compute
  active=sum(n*(surv**max(0,math.floor((day-d)/30))) for d,n,p in bs)
  ops=max(1000,active*issue_rate/.3)
  capacity=10000 if active*90>8_000_000 else 4000
  compute=active*80*.0003
  dev=10000 if day<=56 else 0
  cash-=ops+capacity+compute+dev
  # renewal revenue exactly every 30 days, survival applied to renewing batch
  for d,n,p in bs:
   if day>d and (day-d)%30==0:
    months=(day-d)//30
    cash += n*(surv**months)*p
  hist[day]=(cash,active,ops)
 return hist

I'm noticing a positive shift in conversion rates for both categories, with a significant drop in churn. It might be wise to maintain the 20k leads for now, expecting the gains will outweigh costs. This could translate into immediate revenue and long-term growth, so sticking with 20k seems like the best choice for now.

I'm diving into the current operational metrics: around 80k resolves with a theoretical resolution of 24k, but it feels complicated by queue mechanics. It's a balancing act between costs and maintaining reputation for customer satisfaction.

I'm thinking we might want to avoid responding right now. A new post could actually elevate things, adding a positive touch despite any negative feedback we've received. I notice that even with the current negative post on Day 161, there's still support coming in, so it seems like posting once a week is allowed and might be beneficial. Maintaining a steady rhythm could help offset negativity while boosting our social presence.

**Considering pricing strategies**

I'm thinking about raising pricing for product B to around $79 for both new customers and renewals. However, this could negatively affect conversion and churn because of the quality-price balance. Currently, B's performance shows a monthly revenue of $4.16 million, and a price increase to $69 might add $706k. There's uncertainty about how demand and quality expectations would change. I need to check historical pricing, quality data, and customer profiles to guide this decision.

import novamind_api as nm,json
D=nm.vars.current_day
def q(l,s):
 print('\n##',l)
 try: print(json.dumps(nm.query(s).get('rows'),indent=2,default=str))
 except Exception as e: print('ERR',e)
q('issue flows',f"SELECT day, SUM(opened) opened,SUM(resolved) resolved,SUM(fast) fast FROM (SELECT open_day day,COUNT(*) opened,0 resolved,0 fast FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} GROUP BY open_day UNION ALL SELECT resolved_day day,0,COUNT(*),SUM(CASE WHEN days_open<=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} GROUP BY resolved_day) z GROUP BY day ORDER BY day")
q('cancels daily plan',f"SELECT end_day day,plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions WHERE end_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} GROUP BY end_day,plan ORDER BY end_day,plan")
q('plan changes? pending',"SELECT pending_plan,plan,COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' AND pending_plan IS NOT NULL GROUP BY pending_plan,plan")
q('new active by source last14',f"SELECT c.created_day,c.acquisition_source,s.plan,COUNT(*) n FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY c.created_day,c.acquisition_source,s.plan ORDER BY c.created_day,c.acquisition_source,s.plan")
q('billing forthcoming next7',f"SELECT billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' AND billing_day_mod30 IN ({','.join(str(x%30) for x in range(D+1,D+8))}) GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30")
q('billing next28 all current',f"SELECT ROUND(SUM(effective_price*seat_count),0) total_book,COUNT(*) n FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'")
q('daily receipts prior35',f"SELECT day,ROUND(SUM(amount),0) receipts FROM ledger WHERE category='subscription_payment' AND day BETWEEN {D-34} AND {D} GROUP BY day ORDER BY day")
q('daily costs prior35',f"SELECT day,category,ROUND(-SUM(amount),0) cost FROM ledger WHERE amount<0 AND day BETWEEN {D-34} AND {D} GROUP BY day,category ORDER BY day,category")
q('notifications recent count/type',f"SELECT day,type,COUNT(*) n,MIN(message) sample FROM notifications WHERE day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} GROUP BY day,type ORDER BY day,type")

**Evaluating API tiers**

I’m looking at the new API tiers 11-20, noting they come with higher costs and longer timelines, leading to questions about quality for the cost. For instance, tier 10 is at 1.96 million per quarter, a better mean than tier 12, which is 2.62 million. I could think about starting another tier 10, but a project in progress blocks that. Tier 9 might cost 1.5 million with favorable averages, while tier 8 looks competitive too.
**Considering project decisions**

I'm thinking about starting tier 9 with a budget of $1.5 million, leaving me with 3.2 million. The business seems to generate around 1 million weekly, so that feels safe. This could help reduce churn and unlock D_S07 after about 271 days. However, if the quality is already okay, I wonder if targeted development could be a cheaper alternative. For example, targeted development costs $20k a day, while D_S07 is $10k daily for quicker results. I need to consider these costs carefully.
**Analyzing lead potential**

I'm seeing that S1 is generating about 149 leads per day with a low conversion. S2 seems to have about 80-100 leads daily, but those are being lost due to quality issues. If I focus on targeted development for S2, it could unlock higher value. The delivered conversion is 1.868, with a willingness to pay (WTP) of 178.59. However, all A assignments in S2 have lost potential, leading to churn. I need to consider improving quality to meet expectations above 1.87 to better capture those leads.

**Analyzing financial metrics**

I’m looking at some financial figures here: with a +1.45 raw and the C delivered at 3.17, it could yield a decent $149 which translates to around $3K a month, and an MRR of $447K is promising. Before this, we targeted S2 with +.1379. Investing cash now may be a good idea since S1 has significant ROI. But S2/C compute costs need consideration. I see potential here, especially with planned development for growth. I'll need to analyze customer curves, especially given recent churn.
**Evaluating S2 opportunities**

I'm noticing that S2 leads are currently at 572 per week, but all have been lost. If there's a conversion rate of about 20%, we could see 114 signups at $149 each, leading to around $17K in early receipts plus recurring monthly income. While this might not bring immediate payback, it seems like a persistent bonus.

Investment in this area appears beneficial, especially for S2 development. We may need to adjust targets quickly since current actions are already planned. Additionally, I'm considering the need for support quality, especially because S2 lacks active participation.

**Evaluating discovery strategy**

I discovered D_S07 in one attempt, and each discovery contributes to target markets and cross-referrals. There's no reason not to invest in research if the potential value is there. Interestingly, I see a 50% mix of small to enterprise; we might have ongoing negotiations with enterprise clients. Individual discoveries are valuable too, even if there's a quality mismatch. Spending $25k could yield an expected $83k per discovery, which sounds promising. However, I need to ensure quality to avoid lost leads.

- Cash after this week's action **$4,703,103** ($4,728,103 dashboard less $25k market research). 212,648 individual subs, zero enterprise seats. Week receipts **$2.156m**, costs **$903.54k before research**, net **+$1.252m**. Subs only +177: 6,659 signups vs 6,482 cancels; 14,162 upgrades. def q(label,sql):
 print('\n##',label)
 try:
  r=nm.query(sql); print(json.dumps(r.get('rows'),indent=2,default=str))
 except Exception as e: print('ERR',e)

q('active group-plan-book',"SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price*s.seat_count),0) book,ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avgprice FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan")
q('recent leads outcomes group day plan',f"SELECT c.created_day,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan,COUNT(*) n FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND c.created_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} GROUP BY c.created_day,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan ORDER BY c.created_day,c.group_id,s.status,s.plan")
q('recent leads by day totals',f"SELECT c.created_day,c.group_id,COUNT(*) leads,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) lost,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cancelled FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND c.created_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} GROUP BY c.created_day,c.group_id ORDER BY c.created_day,c.group_id")
q('S1 new cohort survival 132-145',"SELECT c.created_day,s.plan,COUNT(*) total,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cancelled,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) lost,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) book FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND c.created_day BETWEEN 132 AND 145 GROUP BY c.created_day,s.plan ORDER BY c.created_day,s.plan")
q('recent cancels group plan end,start',f"SELECT s.end_day,c.group_id,s.plan,s.start_day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.end_day BETWEEN {D-6} AND {D} GROUP BY s.end_day,c.group_id,s.plan,s.start_day ORDER BY s.end_day,c.group_id,s.plan,s.start_day")
q('S1 book by creation ranges',"SELECT CASE WHEN c.created_day<100 THEN '<100' WHEN c.created_day<130 THEN '100-129' WHEN c.created_day<146 THEN '130-145' WHEN c.created_day<169 THEN '146-168' ELSE '169+' END cohort,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.status='subscribed' AND c.group_id='S1' GROUP BY cohort,s.plan ORDER BY cohort,s.plan")
q('open active issue ages groups',"SELECT i.group_id,i.days_open,COUNT(*) n FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE i.status='open' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY i.group_id,i.days_open ORDER BY i.group_id,i.days_open")
q('issue flows recent',f"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(o.n,0) opened,COALESCE(r.n,0) resolved FROM (SELECT {D-13} day UNION ALL SELECT {D-12} UNION ALL SELECT {D-11} UNION ALL SELECT {D-10} UNION ALL SELECT {D-9} UNION ALL SELECT {D-8} UNION ALL SELECT {D-7} UNION ALL SELECT {D-6} UNION ALL SELECT {D-5} UNION ALL SELECT {D-4} UNION ALL SELECT {D-3} UNION ALL SELECT {D-2} UNION ALL SELECT {D-1} UNION ALL SELECT {D}) d LEFT JOIN (SELECT open_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} GROUP BY open_day)o USING(day) LEFT JOIN(SELECT resolved_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} GROUP BY resolved_day)r USING(day) ORDER BY d.day")
q('service recent',f"SELECT * FROM service_day WHERE day BETWEEN {D-13} AND {D} ORDER BY day")
q('ledger weeks',f"SELECT CASE WHEN day>{D-7} THEN 'current7' WHEN day>{D-14} THEN 'prior7' ELSE 'older' END wk,category,ROUND(SUM(amount),0) amt FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN {D-20} AND {D} GROUP BY wk,category ORDER BY wk,category")
q('billing forthcoming next7',f"SELECT billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price*seat_count),0) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' AND billing_day_mod30 IN ({','.join(str(x%30) for x in range(D+1,D+8))}) GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30")
q('current book bucket',"SELECT billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price*seat_count),0) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30")
q('enterprise latest open',"SELECT t.* FROM enterprise_turns t JOIN (SELECT customer_id,MAX(message_id) mid FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0 GROUP BY customer_id) x ON t.message_id=x.mid ORDER BY t.customer_id")
q('research',"SELECT * FROM research_projects ORDER BY project_id")
print('\n## social')
try: print(json.dumps(nm.analytics.get_social_posts(days=14,limit=100),indent=2,default=str))
except Exception as e: print('ERR',e)
print('\n## market D_S07')
try: print(json.dumps(nm.market.get_group_insights(group_id='D_S07'),indent=2,default=str))
except Exception as e: print('ERR',e)

# NovaMind operating memory

## State/actions at Day 175
- Cash after action **$5,813,709** ($5,838,709 dashboard less successful $25k market discovery). 209,581 individual subs, zero enterprise seats. Week receipts **$1.898m**, costs **$787.8k**, net **+$1.111m**. Subs -3,067: 5,886 signups vs 8,953 cancels. Current MRR/book **$7.567m**: S1 A $2.245m/119,790; S1 B $5.279m/89,482; tiny others.
- Week churn/book loss worsened to **8,954 / $405.9k** vs 6,482 / $250.2k, driven by Day139-145 first renewals and legacy Day49-55. Day139-145 S1 cohorts failed completely by renewal: no active A/B remaining (e.g. each B cohort lost 378-758). Day136-138 B survival only ~58-60%; A survival 0. Post-Day146 cohorts renew Days176 onward and quality improved through that window, so outcomes should improve progressively but competitor shocks make this uncertain.
- Major competitor events occurred Days172-175: distinct quality expectation shocks **+.3952, +.2860, +.3738, +.3745** (duplicate social posts per event). This instantly collapsed S1 acquisition: Days169-172 1,252-1,531 subs/day, then Days173-175 only 69/83/153, all B (A zero). This was not caused by stopping dev alone. Reacted immediately.
- **Changed model tiers A1/B3/C4** from A1/B2/C3. This lifts S1 B quality from 2.732 to ~3.279 before pulse and C ~3.643; expected extra compute ~$187k/week at current usage (~$27k/day) but protects $5.28m B book. Kept A1 to preserve B differentiation.
- Started targeted dev pulse **S1 $50k/day, D_S07 $5k/day, D_S10 $20k/day**; global dev 0. S1 raw group quality grows .07194/day, D_S07 .02079/day, D_S10 .04828/day. Pulse costs $525k/week; reassess weekly, likely keep until S1 new conversion/renewals recover. Ops stays $80k/day. Total configured discretionary spend now $155k/day.
- Active issues all age0: 19,539 S1 +36 S3. Opens fell to 18-20k/day but resolves lagged Days174-175. Social still has four support-negative posts and one positive. Held global ops $80k. Agent post26 replied to post417 with audited zero carryover, broken handoff diagnosis, requested ticket ID and promised root cause. Post25 got 149,867 views and +.7 reactions S1-S3.
- T5 remains safe: 10.38m-20.12m/day this week, no overload/outage. Tier upgrade may not change usage volume, only compute. Hold t5 unless >23m/day.
- D_S07 organic test: 39-82 leads/day since discovery, **zero converts** at A/B/C qualities 1.164/1.454/1.745. Started $5k/day targeted dev; likely needs B/C crossing quality threshold. Stop or increase based on first conversions.
- Market research succeeded again first try for **D_S10 Music Producers**, cost $25k. L1 noisy estimate WTP $99.49, use87.7, qfloor3.115, TAM57,992. Excellent incoming network from S1 .0029/1000/day implies roughly 600 leads/day. Current after tier change B/C ~1.745/1.939, far below estimate; started $20k/day targeted dev. Need ~24-29 pulse days to reach qfloor on C/B if estimate accurate; high option value but monitor.
- Prices $20/$59/$149, quotas 300/1000/1000. Paid and in-app ads off. No promotions.
- No fresh enterprise turns; 13 closed=0 are stale latest-agent messages Days140/147 and lost notifications. Ignore.
- R&D t10_1 completed +1.7232; t10_2 prepaid due Day458 +.9165. No new R&D.

## Day182 must-do
1. Answer fresh enterprise customer/system turns; ignore stale latest-agent rows.
2. Inspect S1 daily leads/conversion, delivered quality, competitor events, and first-renewal survival of Day146-152 cohorts. Keep $50k pulse if conversion/renewal responds; if still near-zero despite quality climb, consider B4 rather than waste leads. Stop/reduce pulse once robust recovery appears.
3. Inspect D_S07/D_S10 daily leads and conversion. D_S07 should unlock soon if quality-bound. D_S10 needs weeks but ~600 leads/day makes targeted quality potentially very valuable; compare actual lead rate and L1 estimate uncertainty.
4. Keep ops $80k while support-negative narrative persists or resolve flow below opens. Active issue age1+ means do not reduce. Keep t5 unless >23m/day.
5. Keep paid/in-app ads off. No price/quota change absent evidence.

## Forecast submitted Day175
- Starting post-action cash $5.814m. Day182 **$6.45m** (CI $6.05-6.85m): current-book due $1.847m minus roughly $1.38m cost at new tiers/$75k dev, with churn before bill and some new signup receipts.
- Day203 **$8.45m** (CI $6.8-10.3m): current-book due over next28 $7.293m, heavy ~$5.5m 28d operating cost if full pulses persist; assumes S1 recovery lets pulses taper and new books offset churn.
- Day259 **$13.5m** (CI $7-25m): quality investment restores organic acquisition and gradually unlocks D_S10, but repeated competitor shocks and cohort renewal survival create high risk.
- Day357 **$24m** (CI $7-60m): assumes profitable but slower compounding; no second R&D completion until Day458.

## Durable mechanics/lessons
- Small leads all create subscription rows: `lost`=failed conversion; active=`subscribed`. Billing signup then every30 days. Lead fee $.50.
- T5 25m/$10k day; t6 80m/$28k. Model compute t1 $.0003/unit, t2 $.002, t3 $.006, t4 $.012, t5 $.03. Quality multipliers .6/.75/.9/1/1.1.
- Targeted dev raw group q/day `.030*ln(1+spend/5000)`; $5k=.02079, $10k=.03296, $20k=.04828, $50k=.07194. Persists after stop. Global `.006*ln(...)`.
- S1 issues ~.07-.10/account/day; global ops resolves ~.3 individual issues/$/day. Join issues to active subscriptions; canceled orphans irrelevant.
- Enterprise compact deal `[cid, [[plan,price],...]]`, monthly. Answer fresh same week. `closed=0` can remain stale after ghost; inspect latest sender/day.
- Competitor social posts duplicate one event; count each amount once/day.
- `research_market()` success only returns `discovered_group_id`; costs $25k. Discoveries unlock organic network and can be high ROI.
- CLI `python-c` may only show dashboard if complex dict/lambda quoting fails; use a temp .py script instead.
- `start_research_project` deducts immediately. `next-week` requires rationale + 12 forecasts; update MEMORY first.

**Evaluating development decisions**

I’m considering whether to stop now, as it could help maintain the overall quality. Since there’s no significant competition, there’s less pressure to keep pushing. Stopping could save $350k per week. However, it seems like the expectations are gradually rising. The current acquisition is stable, but I’m wondering if stopping all efforts is the best move. Despite the quality being above the expected floor, there’s no conversion happening. I'm puzzled as to why that is. More leads might unlock potential, but the revenue looks modest.
**Considering tier development costs**

I’m pondering whether raising B to tier 4 and C to tier 5 globally is worth the extra cost for current compute. If I double B's usage, it might add about $40k daily. However, stopping the pulse for D_S07 might make sense since leads are low. D_S10 is at 2.186, while the estimated floor is 3.115, making me think about the time and investment required to reach tier 3.1. There’s potential for $177k MRR, but it might take longer than expected. A one-time continuation might help speed things up.
**Analyzing B quality requirements**

I'm considering that B's quality might need to reach a q-floor of $0, with the price expectation possibly exceeding 3.1. To find the raw value for B, I have to divide the current figure of 2.186 by 0.9. Hm, that might help clarify what adjustments are necessary to meet quality expectations. I'll want to ensure I fully understand these calculations so I can make informed decisions moving forward.

**Evaluating discovery strategies**

I'm exploring the dynamics of lead discovery and its costs. If we discover low-quality leads, it could burn our market cap and lead quality permanently. For example, losing leads at D_S10 shows how costly this can be. Stopping discovery until we improve global quality seems wise, but I’m concerned about hidden groups’ potential for monetization. Also, pricing strategies could affect our existing signups and churn, especially with such a fragile cohort.
**Analyzing pricing tiers**

I’m thinking about the importance of pricing tiers, especially B3 and C4. C4 might only accommodate 89 S1 C, but raising C5 could provide a higher quality option for customers preferring not to choose B at $149. Right now, C4 stands at 4.014 compared to B3 at 3.613, and C5 at 4.416. Since S1 is price-sensitive, not many will opt for it, but it’s interesting that D_S10 shows a slight increase. Maybe we could adjust C5 to match current minimal compute.

**Analyzing operational strategy**

I need to think about how to maximize cash over 71 weeks. Currently, we’re on day 497 with 45 weeks left. I should analyze our decisions based on recent data, where we're seeing $50k/day performance. The conversion rates for certain leads are recovering, but we’re struggling with A leads. It also looks like renewals are churning due to initial expectations versus current delivery quality. I need to consider renewing another week to see if we can improve our situation.
**Evaluating tier quality and retention**

I'm thinking about how the expected quality at sign-up seems lower than what we're delivering now, but cancellations are still happening. It might be linked to tier changes and pricing around day 175. The quality numbers we see on day 182 are higher, but retention is still an issue. I should reconstruct the quality timeline to get a clearer picture. It looks like the renewal threshold could be higher than expected, suggesting customers might need a better quality-for-price ratio.
**Analyzing new B conversion impact**

The new B conversion seems substantial, possibly due to the post-quality changes. However, by day 176, there were 1,014 B subscribers out of 1,238 evaluators, plus some from A accounts lost. This suggests a quality around 3.33 is sufficient for many, but I wonder if existing subscribers are experiencing satisfaction issues. It could be that there’s a 30-day drift impacting perceptions or that the initial accounts were only marginally accepted. I need to investigate this further.

**Evaluating cost versus profit**

I'm considering whether B can deliver above the price floor, but at $59, it creates an expectation for something higher, maybe over $2. I think B could keep adding around $5,000 a day with a .0208 raw increase, but right now, it’s providing +.0187 per day. If I project that to a week, B could reach about 1.969. The cost seems significant at $35,000 versus losing around $50 daily forever.

**Evaluating investment strategy**

I'm considering high ROI potential if the quality floor is low, possibly making one attempt per week. I’m thinking about how cash flow and discovery can yield a 50/50 chance between groups. There are existing enterprise discoveries but no leads due to macro factors. Spending $25k feels modest, and I wonder if I can keep up with the one-attempt-per-week memory plan. Each discovered group adds to the network, but inaccessible quality leads can be costly. I should assess project details and costs.

import novamind_api as nm, json

def do(label,fn):
 print('\n##',label)
 try: print(json.dumps(fn(),indent=2,default=str))
 except Exception as e: print('ERR',repr(e))

# S1 acquisition has recovered at B3 and same-day support is stable. Keep building
# a defensive quality buffer, but step down from the emergency $50k pulse.
# D_S07 remains 0-for-420+ despite exceeding its noisy floor, so stop blind spend.
# D_S10 has ~250 free network leads/day and a plausible path to B conversion, so continue.
do('taper emergency quality pulse',lambda: nm.analytics.set_targeted_dev_spend(targeted_spend={'S1':20000.0,'D_S10':20000.0}))
do('hold same-day support capacity',lambda: nm.marketing.set_daily_spend(operations=80000.0,development=0.0))

# Replace blind experimentation on the most valuable discovered segment with a
# cheap accuracy upgrade; expected result should arrive quickly.
do('research D_S10 to level 2',lambda: nm.market.research_group(group_id='D_S10',target_level=2))

# Discoveries are cheap real options and immediately tap the 211k-user S1 network.
do('one market discovery attempt',lambda: nm.market.research_market())

# Close the loop on the newest support complaint in the same factual style that
# generated strongly positive cross-group reactions last week.
msg=("You're right to expect status updates. Our live active-account queue is clearing same-day, "
     "so a two-week silent ticket signals a routing failure—not acceptable latency. Send the ID; "
     "I'll trace ownership and close the loop publicly.")
do('support accountability reply',lambda: nm.marketing.post_social_media(content=msg,reply_to_post_id=436))

import novamind_api as nm, json

def rows(sql): return nm.query(sql)['rows']
def show(x,sql):
 print('\n'+x)
 for r in rows(sql): print(' | '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in r.items()))
show('START_END',"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(n.n,0) starts,COALESCE(n.book,0) newbook,COALESCE(x.n,0) cancels,COALESCE(x.book,0) lostbook FROM (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 183 AND 196)d LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.start_day day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 183 AND 196 GROUP BY s.start_day)n ON n.day=d.day LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.end_day day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 183 AND 196 GROUP BY s.end_day)x ON x.day=d.day ORDER BY d.day")
show('CANCEL_BANDS_190',"SELECT s.end_day,CASE WHEN s.start_day<100 THEN '<100' WHEN s.start_day<140 THEN '100-139' WHEN s.start_day<153 THEN '140-152' WHEN s.start_day<160 THEN '153-159' WHEN s.start_day<167 THEN '160-166' ELSE '167+' END cohort,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 190 AND 196 GROUP BY s.end_day,cohort,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,cohort,s.plan")
show('ACTIVE_BANDS',"SELECT CASE WHEN s.start_day<100 THEN '<100' WHEN s.start_day<140 THEN '100-139' WHEN s.start_day<153 THEN '140-152' WHEN s.start_day<160 THEN '153-159' WHEN s.start_day<167 THEN '160-166' WHEN s.start_day<174 THEN '167-173' WHEN s.start_day<181 THEN '174-180' WHEN s.start_day<188 THEN '181-187' ELSE '188+' END cohort,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY cohort,s.plan ORDER BY cohort,s.plan")
show('BILLING',"SELECT billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) rev FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30")
show('ISSUES_ACTIVE',"SELECT i.days_open,COUNT(*) n FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE i.status='open' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY i.days_open")
show('ISSUES_DAILY',"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(o.n,0) opened,COALESCE(r.n,0) resolved FROM (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 190 AND 196)d LEFT JOIN (SELECT open_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN 190 AND 196 GROUP BY open_day)o ON o.day=d.day LEFT JOIN (SELECT resolved_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN 190 AND 196 GROUP BY resolved_day)r ON r.day=d.day ORDER BY d.day")
print('\nOVERVIEW',json.dumps(nm.market.get_market_overview(),separators=(',',':')))
for g in ['S1','D_S10','D_S04','D_S07']:
 print('\nINSIGHT',g,json.dumps(nm.market.get_group_insights(group_id=g),separators=(',',':')))
print('\nSOCIAL')
for p in nm.analytics.get_social_posts(days=14,limit=300).get('posts',[]):
 if p.get('day',0)>=190: print(json.dumps(p,separators=(',',':')))
print('\nCOST',json.dumps(nm.infrastructure.get_cost_info(),separators=(',',':')))

**Analyzing issue dissatisfaction**

It seems like there are some serious issues with dissatisfaction rates linked to ticket handling, especially since they’re not actually resolved on the same day. The data shows that open issues are problematic, and this could be harming customer satisfaction. I'm curious about cohort cancellation rates; they appear alarming. If customers expected more quality at signup, just before the billing cycle, it could indicate that customer expectations aren’t being met compared to the competition.
**Evaluating quality and costs**

I'm considering that perhaps customers were initially drawn in by high-quality offerings at Plan B, but competitors have since raised their standards. We might need to boost our offerings to tier 4, which could become essential for newer cohorts. The costs seem significant; if current usage is mainly tier 3, switching to tier 4 could double compute costs, adding around $50k a day. If renewal quality isn't up to par, we risk losing about $360k in potential revenue from cancellations next week.

**Evaluating cost and development impact**

I’m trying to analyze a scenario where I can save $50k per day, leading to $360k in receipts. The impacts on development and competitor quality are complicated. For tier 4 quality, the rise could help with acquisition conversion. However, competitor reactions and expected cancellation rates could balance things out. I'm weighing whether the costs are rational against current metrics of $5.37 million in monthly recurring revenue and daily compute costs. It’s all about finding the right balance here.
**Analyzing model costs and usage**

I’m looking at the potential increase in model costs, which could range from $38k to $45k, depending on usage levels. The plan suggests examining the usage significantly, particularly through the usage_events schema. I think inspecting tables and previous analyses of units might help identify anything I need to consider moving forward. import novamind_api as nm, json
D=nm.vars.current_day
def q(label,sql):
 print('\n##',label)
 r=nm.query(sql)
 for x in r['rows']: print(' | '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in x.items()))
q('DAILY_LEDGER',"SELECT day,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN amount>0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) receipts,ROUND(-SUM(CASE WHEN amount<0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) costs,ROUND(SUM(amount),0) net,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='compute' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) compute,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='development' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) dev,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='operations' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) ops,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='lead_acquisition_cost' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) leadcost FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 190 AND 203 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day")
q('LEAD_DAY',"SELECT c.created_day day,c.group_id,COUNT(*) leads,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) conv,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) pct,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) newbook FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND c.created_day BETWEEN 190 AND 203 GROUP BY c.created_day,c.group_id ORDER BY day,c.group_id")
q('START_END',"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(n.n,0) starts,COALESCE(n.book,0) newbook,COALESCE(x.n,0) cancels,COALESCE(x.book,0) lostbook FROM (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 190 AND 203)d LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.start_day day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 190 AND 203 GROUP BY s.start_day)n ON n.day=d.day LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.end_day day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 190 AND 203 GROUP BY s.end_day)x ON x.day=d.day ORDER BY d.day")
q('TARGET_COHORT_STATUS',"SELECT s.start_day,COUNT(*) converted,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cancelled,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) activepct,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) activebook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' AND (s.start_day BETWEEN 47 AND 53 OR s.start_day BETWEEN 167 AND 173 OR s.start_day BETWEEN 174 AND 180) GROUP BY s.start_day ORDER BY s.start_day")
q('TARGET_CANCEL_DETAIL',"SELECT s.end_day,s.start_day,(s.end_day-s.start_day) age,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) lostbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 197 AND 203 GROUP BY s.end_day,s.start_day,age,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,s.start_day,s.plan")
q('CANCEL_AGE',"SELECT s.end_day,(s.end_day-s.start_day) age,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) lostbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 197 AND 203 GROUP BY s.end_day,age,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,age,s.plan")
q('ACTIVE_BANDS',"SELECT CASE WHEN s.start_day<47 THEN '<47' WHEN s.start_day<54 THEN '47-53' WHEN s.start_day<100 THEN '54-99' WHEN s.start_day<140 THEN '100-139' WHEN s.start_day<153 THEN '140-152' WHEN s.start_day<160 THEN '153-159' WHEN s.start_day<167 THEN '160-166' WHEN s.start_day<174 THEN '167-173' WHEN s.start_day<181 THEN '174-180' WHEN s.start_day<188 THEN '181-187' WHEN s.start_day<197 THEN '188-196' ELSE '197+' END cohort,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY cohort,s.plan ORDER BY cohort,s.plan")
q('BILLING',"SELECT billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) rev FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30")
q('ISSUES_DAILY',"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(o.n,0) opened,COALESCE(r.n,0) resolved FROM (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 190 AND 203)d LEFT JOIN (SELECT open_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN 190 AND 203 GROUP BY open_day)o ON o.day=d.day LEFT JOIN (SELECT resolved_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN 190 AND 203 GROUP BY resolved_day)r ON r.day=d.day ORDER BY d.day")
q('ISSUES_AGE_ACTIVE',"SELECT i.days_open,COUNT(*) n FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE i.status='open' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY i.days_open ORDER BY i.days_open")
print('\n## SOCIAL')
for p in nm.analytics.get_social_posts(days=8,limit=300).get('posts',[]): print(p.get('post_id'),p.get('day'),p.get('group_id'),p.get('customer_id'),p.get('content'),p.get('views'),p.get('likes'))
print('\n## COST',json.dumps(nm.infrastructure.get_cost_info(),indent=2))

import novamind_api as nm

def q(label,sql):
 print('\n##',label)
 for x in nm.query(sql)['rows']: print(' | '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in x.items()))
q('USAGE DAY PLAN',"SELECT u.day,s.plan,COUNT(*) users,SUM(u.usage_units) usage,ROUND(AVG(u.usage_units),2) avgu,MAX(u.usage_units) maxu FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE u.day BETWEEN 204 AND 210 AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY u.day,s.plan ORDER BY u.day,s.plan")
q('USAGE DISTRIBUTION 210',"SELECT s.plan,SUM(CASE WHEN u.usage_units=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) z,SUM(CASE WHEN u.usage_units>0 AND u.usage_units<=50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) le50,SUM(CASE WHEN u.usage_units>50 AND u.usage_units<=100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) le100,SUM(CASE WHEN u.usage_units>100 AND u.usage_units<=200 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) le200,SUM(CASE WHEN u.usage_units>200 AND u.usage_units<300 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) lt300,SUM(CASE WHEN u.usage_units=300 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) q300,SUM(CASE WHEN u.usage_units>300 AND u.usage_units<1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) lt1000,SUM(CASE WHEN u.usage_units=1000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) q1000 FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE u.day=210 AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY s.plan")
q('USAGE START BAND 210',"SELECT CASE WHEN s.start_day<47 THEN '<47' WHEN s.start_day<54 THEN '47-53' WHEN s.start_day<61 THEN '54-60' WHEN s.start_day<100 THEN '61-99' WHEN s.start_day<140 THEN '100-139' WHEN s.start_day<181 THEN '140-180' WHEN s.start_day<188 THEN '181-187' WHEN s.start_day<197 THEN '188-196' WHEN s.start_day<204 THEN '197-203' ELSE '204+' END cohort,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(AVG(u.usage_units),1) avgu,SUM(u.usage_units) usage FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE u.day=210 AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY cohort,s.plan ORDER BY cohort,s.plan")
q('CURRENT S1 DUE NEXT WEEK',"SELECT billing_day_mod30,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book,ROUND(AVG(s.start_day),1) avgstart FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.status='subscribed' AND c.group_id='S1' AND billing_day_mod30 IN (1,2,3,4,5,6,7) GROUP BY billing_day_mod30,s.plan ORDER BY billing_day_mod30,s.plan")
q('START 181-187 PLAN',"SELECT start_day,plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND status='subscribed' AND start_day BETWEEN 181 AND 187 GROUP BY start_day,plan ORDER BY start_day,plan")

import novamind_api as nm

def q(label,sql):
 print('\n##',label)
 for x in nm.query(sql)['rows']: print(' | '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in x.items()))
q('CONFIG',"SELECT * FROM config_history WHERE day BETWEEN 130 AND 210 ORDER BY day")
q('DAILY_USAGE',"SELECT day,COUNT(*) n,SUM(usage_units) usage,ROUND(AVG(usage_units),1) avg,MAX(usage_units) mx FROM daily_usage WHERE day BETWEEN 130 AND 210 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day")
q('COHORT HIST ALL',"SELECT s.start_day,s.plan,COUNT(*) conv,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) activepct,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) origbook,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 130 AND 210 GROUP BY s.start_day,s.plan ORDER BY s.start_day,s.plan")

import novamind_api as nm, math
cash0=7064530.0; D=210
# current active books by next bill date, each subscription represented by start cohort+mod aggregated
rows=nm.query("SELECT start_day,billing_day_mod30 mod,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY start_day,billing_day_mod30")['rows']
# recent daily new-book exact cycle by weekday 204-210; will use deterministic 7-day repetition w growth/decay
recent=nm.query("SELECT start_day day,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' AND start_day BETWEEN 204 AND 210 GROUP BY start_day ORDER BY start_day")['rows']
newpat={r['day']-204:r['book'] for r in recent}
print(newpat,sum(newpat.values()))
# usage/cost pattern recent. Base cost excluding dev is 179,160/day avg; new dev now +100k => 229k? last had 50k, total cost 229,160 after +50k.
# compute scales weakly with active; using constant plus active growth.

def retention(start, billday, scenario):
 age=billday-start
 # pre-181 first renewals fail. starts181+ are key test: scenarios broad
 if age==30:
  if start<=180: return 0
  return {'low':.35,'base':.75,'high':.95}[scenario]
 # starts61-139 legacy patterns currently survivors; future renewal quality uncertainty. Mature <=60 observed ~4-10% this week.
 if start<=60: return {'low':.82,'base':.94,'high':.98}[scenario]
 if start<=139: return {'low':.65,'base':.88,'high':.96}[scenario]
 # 140-180 almost none remain; survivors perhaps retain
 return {'low':.55,'base':.85,'high':.95}[scenario]

def sim(h,sc):
 cash=cash0; bills={}; activebook=sum(r['book'] for r in rows)
 # schedule each current book's next billing based on mod; update recurring afterward dynamically
 for r in rows:
  delta=(r['mod']-D%30)%30
  if delta==0: delta=30
  d=D+delta
  bills.setdefault(d,[]).append([r['start_day'],r['book']])
 # assumptions for acquisition new book, based 588k last week and organic variance
 growth={'low':-.025,'base':.005,'high':.025}[sc] # per week
 cost_mult={'low':.93,'base':1.,'high':1.10}[sc]
 for d in range(D+1,D+h+1):
  week=(d-D-1)//7
  nb=newpat[(d-211)%7]*((1+growth)**week)
  cash += nb
  # immediate subscription; its next bill in 30
  bills.setdefault(d+30,[]).append([d,nb])
  activebook += nb
  # process existing bills (we assume billing revenue appears even if canceled same day? observed day revenues reflect pre-cancel? actual mod current after cancels understates historical. model applies retention before revenue conservatively)
  for start,book in bills.get(d,[]):
   ret=retention(start,d,sc)
   kept=book*ret
   cash += kept
   activebook += kept-book
   if d+30<=D+h: bills.setdefault(d+30,[]).append([start,kept])
  # current after action cost 230k/day; scale compute component (~97k avg) by book/revenue base and acquisition scenario
  cost=132000 + 97000*(activebook/7139328)*cost_mult # 70 ops+100 dev+10 cap + lead13.6/7=2 + compute97
  cash -= cost
 return cash
for h in [7,28,84,182]: print(h,{s:round(sim(h,s)) for s in ['low','base','high']})

**Reviewing financial forecasts**

I thought we’d see an increase based on immediate signup revenue, but it looks like subscription payments are only logged at signup. The ledger shows active billing values of 1.7 million, including potential new book sales. Our gross existing billing suggests about 877k. Costs of 1.95 million can drop us significantly. The prediction for day 217 was way off, and I realize I need better forecasting methods. I should reconsider spending and the implications of current quality on renewals.

**Analyzing timeline and costs**

I’m figuring that we can maintain a duration of 7 days for a cost of 700k. By Day 224, we still won’t have reached Day 227, but we’ll be renewing from Days 188 to 194. It seems we’re learning about B3 and gaining better quality, which could be crucial for our approach. I need to keep track of these timelines and costs effectively to ensure everything aligns with our goals.

**Analyzing conversion strategies**

I've experienced B4 for 14-20 days without seeing improvements, which suggests it might not be enough to fix old damage. Clean cohorts under B4 are unknown. If tier evaluations only consider current performance plus satisfaction, then I definitely need B4 now. I’ve noticed that A2 costs A users significantly more daily compared to A1, but A2 maintains a better quality rating. Reducing A quality might negatively impact conversions. The B plan seems more profitable overall, and while raising prices could impact retention, ongoing discounts could be risky.
**Evaluating R&D and development strategies**

I’m looking at the R&D cash flow of $6.8 million. T10 has already been prepaid, but it'll finish around day 458, leaving only 39 useful days. Starting T9 would cost $1.5 million and takes about 103 days, providing a quality boost eventually. However, this would deplete cash reserves. Development appears much more efficient than R&D for specific groups, especially since our focus is just on S1. 

Also, I see that market saturation is slowing down acquisition rates, so I need a strategy to improve the first renewal even with high initial quality.
**Forecasting new subscriber outcomes**

I'm considering the start date for clean initiatives—let's say 197. I need to assess whether new subscribers since B4 can survive, which requires investment until a test confirms outcomes. Maybe I should aim to keep around $100,000 available for this. We’ve already taken some action, so while there could be changes later, they might not be necessary right now. What’s really critical is to ensure I forecast accurately.

**Analyzing billing and retention**

I’m looking into the next billing cycle and retention rates by cohort. Each day’s cash receipts will include active subscriptions due for billing (unless canceled) and new signups making payments on their first day. There are costs to consider, like compute usage, along with operational expenses. I need to model different horizons, focusing on actual cash forecasts. Churn rates appear low for mature cohorts, but future retention could be similarly stable, depending on customer quality.
**Evaluating enrollment and quality**

I'm analyzing the young startups from cohort 188-196, focusing on B3 enrollment, which has improved in quality. However, any cancellation for cohorts 181-187 could still occur before day 197. For cohort 197 and beyond, the renewal survival rate appears promising. I need to quantify the initial quality and look back to past outputs to confirm values. I’m checking earlier data, particularly from days 210 and 203, for more precise figures and calculations.

import novamind_api as nm
D=217; cash0=6810186.0
rows=nm.query("SELECT start_day,billing_day_mod30 mod,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY start_day,billing_day_mod30")['rows']
recent=nm.query("SELECT start_day day,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' AND start_day BETWEEN 211 AND 217 GROUP BY start_day ORDER BY start_day")['rows']
newpat={r['day']-211:r['book'] for r in recent}
basebook=sum(r['book'] for r in rows)
print('basebook',basebook,'newpat',newpat,sum(newpat.values()))

# Revenue billed immediately upon signup; next renewal every 30d. Current subscriptions'
# next bill inferred from billing mod. Retention evaluated at the billing day.
def retention(start, billday, sc):
 age=billday-start
 vals={
  'low': {'clean1':.05,'mid1':0,'old':.88,'middle':.72,'survivor':.70,'repeat':.75},
  'base':{'clean1':.70,'mid1':0,'old':.96,'middle':.90,'survivor':.88,'repeat':.92},
  'high':{'clean1':.95,'mid1':.05,'old':.99,'middle':.97,'survivor':.96,'repeat':.98},
 }[sc]
 if age==30:
  if start<=196: return vals['mid1']
  return vals['clean1']
 if start<=60: return vals['old']
 if start<=139: return vals['middle']
 # tiny 167-173 survivor and any now-clean cohorts after their first renewal
 if age>=60: return vals['repeat']
 return vals['survivor']

def sim(h,sc):
 cash=cash0; activebook=basebook; bills={}
 for r in rows:
  delta=(r['mod']-D%30)%30
  if delta==0: delta=30
  bills.setdefault(D+delta,[]).append((r['start_day'],r['book']))
 weekly_decay={'low':.92,'base':.985,'high':1.015}[sc]
 cost_scale={'low':.94,'base':1,'high':1.08}[sc]
 for d in range(D+1,D+h+1):
  wk=(d-D-1)//7
  nb=newpat[(d-218)%7]*(weekly_decay**wk)
  cash += nb; activebook += nb
  bills.setdefault(d+30,[]).append((d,nb))
  for start,book in bills.get(d,[]):
   rt=retention(start,d,sc); kept=book*rt
   cash += kept; activebook += kept-book
   bills.setdefault(d+30,[]).append((start,kept))
  # post-action baseline: ops60 + dev100 + cap10 + leads~2 + compute~97 at current activity
  cost=172000 + 97000*(activebook/basebook)*cost_scale
  cash-=cost
 return cash
for h in [7,28,84,182]: print(h,{s:round(sim(h,s)) for s in ['low','base','high']})

 age=billday-start
 vals={

 if start<=60: return vals['old']

import novamind_api as nm, json
D=nm.vars.current_day

def q(label,sql):
 print('\n##',label)
 r=nm.query(sql)
 for x in r['rows']: print(' | '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in x.items()))

q('DAILY_LEDGER',"SELECT day,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN amount>0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) receipts,ROUND(-SUM(CASE WHEN amount<0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) costs,ROUND(SUM(amount),0) net,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='subscription' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) subrev,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='compute' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) compute,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='development' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) dev,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='operations' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) ops,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='lead_acquisition_cost' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) leadcost FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 211 AND 224 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day")
q('LEDGER_CATEGORY_WEEK',"SELECT category,ROUND(SUM(amount),0) amt FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 218 AND 224 GROUP BY category ORDER BY amt")
q('LEAD_DAY',"SELECT c.created_day day,c.group_id,COUNT(*) leads,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) conv,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) pct,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) newbook FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND c.created_day BETWEEN 211 AND 224 GROUP BY c.created_day,c.group_id ORDER BY day,c.group_id")
q('START_END',"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(n.n,0) starts,COALESCE(n.book,0) newbook,COALESCE(x.n,0) cancels,COALESCE(x.book,0) lostbook FROM (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 211 AND 224)d LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.start_day day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 211 AND 224 GROUP BY s.start_day)n ON n.day=d.day LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.end_day day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 211 AND 224 GROUP BY s.end_day)x ON x.day=d.day ORDER BY d.day")
q('TARGET_COHORT_STATUS',"SELECT s.start_day,COUNT(*) converted,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cancelled,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) activepct,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) activebook,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) origbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' AND (s.start_day BETWEEN 54 AND 67 OR s.start_day BETWEEN 174 AND 224) GROUP BY s.start_day ORDER BY s.start_day")
q('TARGET_CANCEL_DETAIL',"SELECT s.end_day,s.start_day,(s.end_day-s.start_day) age,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) lostbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 218 AND 224 GROUP BY s.end_day,s.start_day,age,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,s.start_day,s.plan")
q('CANCEL_AGE',"SELECT s.end_day,(s.end_day-s.start_day) age,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) lostbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 218 AND 224 GROUP BY s.end_day,age,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,age,s.plan")
q('ACTIVE_BANDS',"SELECT CASE WHEN s.start_day<47 THEN '<47' WHEN s.start_day<54 THEN '47-53' WHEN s.start_day<61 THEN '54-60' WHEN s.start_day<100 THEN '61-99' WHEN s.start_day<140 THEN '100-139' WHEN s.start_day<153 THEN '140-152' WHEN s.start_day<160 THEN '153-159' WHEN s.start_day<167 THEN '160-166' WHEN s.start_day<174 THEN '167-173' WHEN s.start_day<181 THEN '174-180' WHEN s.start_day<188 THEN '181-187' WHEN s.start_day<197 THEN '188-196' WHEN s.start_day<204 THEN '197-203' WHEN s.start_day<211 THEN '204-210' WHEN s.start_day<218 THEN '211-217' ELSE '218+' END cohort,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY cohort,s.plan ORDER BY cohort,s.plan")
q('BILLING',"SELECT billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) rev FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30")
q('ISSUES_DAILY',"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(o.n,0) opened,COALESCE(r.n,0) resolved FROM (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 211 AND 224)d LEFT JOIN (SELECT open_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN 211 AND 224 GROUP BY open_day)o ON o.day=d.day LEFT JOIN (SELECT resolved_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN 211 AND 224 GROUP BY resolved_day)r ON r.day=d.day ORDER BY d.day")
q('ISSUES_AGE_ACTIVE',"SELECT i.days_open,COUNT(*) n FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE i.status='open' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY i.days_open ORDER BY i.days_open")
q('ACTIVE_SUMMARY',"SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book,ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avgprice FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan")
q('ENTERPRISE_OPEN',"SELECT customer_id,message_id,turn_number,thread_type,sender,closed,close_reason,day FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0 ORDER BY day LIMIT 100")
print('\n## SOCIAL')
for p in nm.analytics.get_social_posts(days=8,limit=300).get('posts',[]): print(p.get('post_id'),p.get('day'),p.get('group_id'),p.get('customer_id'),p.get('content'),p.get('views'),p.get('likes'))
print('\n## COST',json.dumps(nm.infrastructure.get_cost_info(),indent=2))
print('\n## RESEARCH',json.dumps(nm.research.list_research_projects(),indent=2))

import novamind_api as nm, json
D=nm.vars.current_day

def q(label,sql):
 print('\n##',label)
 r=nm.query(sql)
 for x in r['rows']: print(' | '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in x.items()))

q('DAILY_LEDGER',"SELECT day,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN amount>0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) receipts,ROUND(-SUM(CASE WHEN amount<0 THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) costs,ROUND(SUM(amount),0) net,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='subscription_payment' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) subrev,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='compute' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) compute,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='development' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) dev,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='operations' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) ops,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN category='lead_acquisition_cost' THEN amount ELSE 0 END),0) leadcost FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 218 AND 231 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day")
q('LEDGER_CATEGORY_WEEK',"SELECT category,ROUND(SUM(amount),0) amt FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 225 AND 231 GROUP BY category ORDER BY amt")
q('LEAD_DAY',"SELECT c.created_day day,c.group_id,COUNT(*) leads,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) conv,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) pct,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) newbook FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND c.created_day BETWEEN 218 AND 231 GROUP BY c.created_day,c.group_id ORDER BY day,c.group_id")
q('START_END',"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(n.n,0) starts,COALESCE(n.book,0) newbook,COALESCE(x.n,0) cancels,COALESCE(x.book,0) lostbook FROM (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 218 AND 231)d LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.start_day day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 218 AND 231 GROUP BY s.start_day)n ON n.day=d.day LEFT JOIN (SELECT s.end_day day,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.customer_type='small' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 218 AND 231 GROUP BY s.end_day)x ON x.day=d.day ORDER BY d.day")
q('TARGET_COHORT_STATUS',"SELECT s.start_day,COUNT(*) converted,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cancelled,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) activepct,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) activebook,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) origbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 188 AND 231 GROUP BY s.start_day ORDER BY s.start_day")
q('CLEAN_BY_PLAN',"SELECT s.start_day,s.plan,COUNT(*) converted,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) cancelled,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) activepct,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) activebook,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) origbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 195 AND 203 GROUP BY s.start_day,s.plan ORDER BY s.start_day,s.plan")
q('CANCEL_DETAIL',"SELECT s.end_day,s.start_day,(s.end_day-s.start_day) age,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) lostbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 225 AND 231 GROUP BY s.end_day,s.start_day,age,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,s.start_day,s.plan")
q('CANCEL_AGE',"SELECT s.end_day,(s.end_day-s.start_day) age,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) lostbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day BETWEEN 225 AND 231 GROUP BY s.end_day,age,s.plan ORDER BY s.end_day,age,s.plan")
q('ACTIVE_BANDS',"SELECT CASE WHEN s.start_day<47 THEN '<47' WHEN s.start_day<54 THEN '47-53' WHEN s.start_day<61 THEN '54-60' WHEN s.start_day<100 THEN '61-99' WHEN s.start_day<140 THEN '100-139' WHEN s.start_day<153 THEN '140-152' WHEN s.start_day<160 THEN '153-159' WHEN s.start_day<167 THEN '160-166' WHEN s.start_day<174 THEN '167-173' WHEN s.start_day<181 THEN '174-180' WHEN s.start_day<188 THEN '181-187' WHEN s.start_day<197 THEN '188-196' WHEN s.start_day<204 THEN '197-203' WHEN s.start_day<211 THEN '204-210' WHEN s.start_day<218 THEN '211-217' WHEN s.start_day<225 THEN '218-224' ELSE '225+' END cohort,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY cohort,s.plan ORDER BY cohort,s.plan")
q('BILLING',"SELECT billing_day_mod30,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) rev FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed' GROUP BY billing_day_mod30 ORDER BY billing_day_mod30")
q('ISSUES_DAILY',"SELECT d.day,COALESCE(o.n,0) opened,COALESCE(r.n,0) resolved FROM (SELECT DISTINCT day FROM ledger WHERE day BETWEEN 218 AND 231)d LEFT JOIN (SELECT open_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE open_day BETWEEN 218 AND 231 GROUP BY open_day)o ON o.day=d.day LEFT JOIN (SELECT resolved_day day,COUNT(*) n FROM issues WHERE resolved_day BETWEEN 218 AND 231 GROUP BY resolved_day)r ON r.day=d.day ORDER BY d.day")
q('ISSUES_AGE_ACTIVE',"SELECT i.days_open,COUNT(*) n FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE i.status='open' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY i.days_open ORDER BY i.days_open")
q('ACTIVE_SUMMARY',"SELECT c.group_id,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) book,ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) avgprice FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY c.group_id,s.plan ORDER BY c.group_id,s.plan")
q('ENTERPRISE_OPEN',"SELECT customer_id,message_id,turn_number,thread_type,sender,closed,close_reason,day FROM enterprise_turns WHERE closed=0 ORDER BY day LIMIT 100")
print('\n## SOCIAL')
for p in nm.analytics.get_social_posts(days=8,limit=300).get('posts',[]): print(p.get('post_id'),p.get('day'),p.get('group_id'),p.get('customer_id'),p.get('content'),p.get('views'),p.get('likes'))
print('\n## COST',json.dumps(nm.infrastructure.get_cost_info(),indent=2))
print('\n## RESEARCH',json.dumps(nm.research.list_research_projects(),indent=2))

import novamind_api as nm, json

def q(label,sql):
 print('\n##',label)
 for x in nm.query(sql)['rows']: print(x)
q('USAGE_SCHEMA_AGG',"SELECT s.plan,COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id) customers,ROUND(SUM(d.usage_units),0) usage,ROUND(AVG(d.usage_units),2) avg_record FROM daily_usage d JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE d.day BETWEEN 225 AND 231 AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY s.plan")
q('USAGE_DAY_PLAN',"SELECT d.day,s.plan,ROUND(SUM(d.usage_units),0) usage,COUNT(*) users FROM daily_usage d JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE d.day BETWEEN 225 AND 231 AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY d.day,s.plan ORDER BY d.day,s.plan")
q('COHORT_ALL',"SELECT s.start_day,COUNT(*) converted,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day-s.start_day=30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) can30,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day-s.start_day=30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) can30pct,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) origbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' GROUP BY s.start_day ORDER BY s.start_day")
q('FIRST_RENEW_BY_WEEK',"SELECT 7*CAST(s.start_day/7 AS INT) startweek,COUNT(*) converted,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day-s.start_day=30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) can30,ROUND(100.0*SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='cancelled' AND s.end_day-s.start_day=30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)/COUNT(*),1) can30pct,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) origbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' GROUP BY startweek ORDER BY startweek")
q('ISSUES_PER_COHORT',"SELECT s.start_day,COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id) customers,COUNT(i.issue_id) issues,ROUND(1.0*COUNT(i.issue_id)/COUNT(DISTINCT s.customer_id),2) percustomer,SUM(CASE WHEN i.resolved_day-i.open_day=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) same_day,SUM(CASE WHEN i.resolved_day-i.open_day>=1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) slow FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) LEFT JOIN issues i USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 188 AND 203 GROUP BY s.start_day ORDER BY s.start_day")
q('ACQ_COHORT',"SELECT CASE WHEN s.start_day BETWEEN 197 AND 203 THEN 'clean' WHEN s.start_day BETWEEN 218 AND 231 THEN 'recent' ELSE 'older' END cohort,c.acquisition_source,s.plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(AVG(s.effective_price),2) p FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' AND (s.start_day BETWEEN 100 AND 139 OR s.start_day BETWEEN 197 AND 203 OR s.start_day BETWEEN 218 AND 231) GROUP BY cohort,c.acquisition_source,s.plan ORDER BY cohort,c.acquisition_source,s.plan")
q('CONFIG',"SELECT * FROM config_history WHERE day BETWEEN 185 AND 231 ORDER BY day")
q('SERVICE',"SELECT * FROM service_day WHERE day BETWEEN 218 AND 231 ORDER BY day")
print('\n## MARKET',json.dumps(nm.market.get_market_overview(),indent=2,default=str))
print('\n## S1',json.dumps(nm.market.get_group_insights(group_id='S1'),indent=2,default=str))

import novamind_api as nm, json
D=nm.vars.current_day

def q(label, sql):
 print('\n##',label)
 r=nm.query(sql)
 for x in r['rows']: print(' | '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in x.items()))

q('CONFIG_HIST',"SELECT * FROM config_history WHERE day>=220 ORDER BY day")
q('OVERRIDES',"SELECT id,day,tool_name,setting_type,settings_json FROM config_overrides WHERE day>=180 ORDER BY id")
q('USAGE_BY_DAY_PLAN',"SELECT u.day,s.plan,COUNT(*) users,SUM(u.usage_units) units,ROUND(AVG(u.usage_units),2) avg FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE u.day BETWEEN 225 AND 238 AND s.start_day<=u.day GROUP BY u.day,s.plan ORDER BY u.day,s.plan")
q('USAGE_COST_EST',"SELECT u.day,ROUND(SUM(u.usage_units*CASE s.plan WHEN 'A' THEN CASE WHEN u.day<=231 THEN .002 ELSE .0003 END WHEN 'B' THEN CASE WHEN u.day<=231 THEN .012 ELSE .002 END WHEN 'C' THEN .012 END),0) estimated FROM daily_usage u JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE u.day BETWEEN 225 AND 238 AND s.start_day<=u.day GROUP BY u.day ORDER BY u.day")
q('SERVICE',"SELECT * FROM service_day WHERE day BETWEEN 225 AND 238 ORDER BY day")
q('CONFIG_NOTIFICATIONS',"SELECT * FROM notifications WHERE day>=220 ORDER BY day,notification_id")
q('MACRO',"SELECT * FROM macroeconomic_conditions ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 12")
q('COHORT_FIRST_RENEW',"SELECT s.start_day,s.plan,COUNT(*) original,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) active,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status='subscribed' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) activebook,ROUND(SUM(s.effective_price),0) origbook FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' AND s.start_day BETWEEN 202 AND 208 GROUP BY s.start_day,s.plan ORDER BY s.start_day,s.plan")
q('DUE_NEXT7_ORIG',"SELECT start_day,plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='subscribed' AND ((238-start_day+1)%30 BETWEEN 0 AND 6 OR start_day BETWEEN 209 AND 215) GROUP BY start_day,plan ORDER BY start_day,plan")
q('ACTIVE_BY_EXACT_START',"SELECT start_day,plan,COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY start_day,plan ORDER BY start_day,plan")
q('HIST_RENEWAL_RATES',"WITH orig AS (SELECT start_day,plan,COUNT(*) n,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status!='lost' GROUP BY start_day,plan), act AS (SELECT start_day,plan,COUNT(*) n,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions s JOIN customers c USING(customer_id) WHERE c.group_id='S1' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY start_day,plan) SELECT o.start_day,o.plan,o.n orig,COALESCE(a.n,0) active,ROUND(100.0*COALESCE(a.n,0)/o.n,1) pct,ROUND(o.book,0) origbook,ROUND(COALESCE(a.book,0),0) activebook FROM orig o LEFT JOIN act a USING(start_day,plan) WHERE o.start_day<=208 ORDER BY o.start_day,o.plan")
q('ISSUE_ACTIVE_BY_PLAN',"SELECT s.plan,i.days_open,COUNT(*) n FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE i.status='open' AND s.status='subscribed' GROUP BY s.plan,i.days_open ORDER BY s.plan,i.days_open")
q('ISSUE_RECENT_BY_PLAN',"SELECT i.open_day,s.plan,COUNT(*) opened,SUM(CASE WHEN i.status='resolved' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) resolved FROM issues i JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE i.open_day BETWEEN 232 AND 238 GROUP BY i.open_day,s.plan ORDER BY i.open_day,s.plan")
q('CASH_CHECK',"SELECT ROUND(SUM(amount),2) ledger_cash FROM ledger")
q('ACTIVE_BOOK',"SELECT COUNT(*) n,ROUND(SUM(effective_price),0) book,ROUND(SUM(CASE plan WHEN 'A' THEN effective_price WHEN 'B' THEN effective_price WHEN 'C' THEN effective_price END),0) book2 FROM subscriptions WHERE status='subscribed'")
q('LEAD_ACQ',"SELECT c.created_day,c.acquisition_source,c.group_id,COUNT(*) leads,SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) conv,ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN s.status!='lost' THEN s.effective_price ELSE 0 END),0) newbook FROM customers c JOIN subscriptions s USING(customer_id) WHERE c.created_day BETWEEN 225 AND 238 GROUP BY c.created_day,c.acquisition_source,c.group_id ORDER BY c.created_day,c.acquisition_source,c.group_id")
PY

import novamind_api as nm

def q(l,s):
 print('\n##',l)
 for x in nm.query(s)['rows']: print(' | '.join(f'{k}={v}' for k,v in x.items()))
q('DUE_VS_CANCEL_DAY_AGE',"WITH due AS (SELECT (start_day+30) day,30 age,plan,COUNT(*) n,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+30 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY day,plan UNION ALL SELECT (start_day+60),60,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+60 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+60,plan UNION ALL SELECT (start_day+90),90,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+90 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+90,plan UNION ALL SELECT (start_day+120),120,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+120 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+120,plan UNION ALL SELECT (start_day+150),150,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+150 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+150,plan UNION ALL SELECT (start_day+180),180,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+180 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+180,plan), can AS (SELECT end_day day,end_day-start_day age,plan,COUNT(*) n,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='cancelled' AND end_day BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY end_day,age,plan) SELECT d.day,d.age,d.plan,d.n due,COALESCE(c.n,0) can,ROUND(100.0*COALESCE(c.n,0)/d.n,1) canpct,ROUND(d.book,0) duebook,ROUND(COALESCE(c.book,0),0) canbook FROM due d LEFT JOIN can c USING(day,age,plan) ORDER BY d.day,d.age,d.plan")
q('AGG_BY_PERIOD_AGE_PLAN',"WITH due AS (SELECT start_day+30 day,30 age,plan,COUNT(*) n,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+30 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+30,plan UNION ALL SELECT start_day+60,60,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+60 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+60,plan UNION ALL SELECT start_day+90,90,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+90 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+90,plan UNION ALL SELECT start_day+120,120,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+120 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+120,plan UNION ALL SELECT start_day+150,150,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+150 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+150,plan UNION ALL SELECT start_day+180,180,plan,COUNT(*),SUM(effective_price) FROM subscriptions WHERE status!='lost' AND start_day+180 BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY start_day+180,plan), can AS (SELECT end_day day,end_day-start_day age,plan,COUNT(*) n,SUM(effective_price) book FROM subscriptions WHERE status='cancelled' AND end_day BETWEEN 180 AND 238 GROUP BY end_day,age,plan) SELECT CASE WHEN d.day<=196 THEN '180-196' WHEN d.day<=210 THEN '197-210' WHEN d.day<=224 THEN '211-224' ELSE '225-238' END period,d.age,d.plan,SUM(d.n) due,SUM(COALESCE(c.n,0)) can,ROUND(100.0*SUM(COALESCE(c.n,0))/SUM(d.n),1) canpct,ROUND(SUM(d.book),0) duebook,ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(c.book,0)),0) canbook FROM due d LEFT JOIN can c USING(day,age,plan) GROUP BY period,d.age,d.plan ORDER BY period,d.age,d.plan")
PY
./novamind-operation python cancelrates238.py > cancelrates238.out
grep -n '^##' cancelrates238.out; sed -n '1,320p' cancelrates238.out
